messages.author: 8cab02bd36843a0b
messages.subject: switch.order abuse?
parts:
Dear Prof Broman,
I’am trying to construct two linkage maps for two mapping populations: F2 and pseudo BC. Using R/qtl (4-way cross option in both cases), I created two separate maps of these populations. From the database, R/qtl selected some markers (221 and 219 respectively) and created two linkage maps with finally - 65 markers (for F2) and 62 markers (for BC). Working on creation of linkage groups, I took into account the value of parameters like: numbers of obligate crossovers, LOD score and chromosome length. In both maps, 50% of the used markers are identical but their order is not the same, p.ex. group 1 in population F2 is “compatible” (= consists of the same markers) like group 6 in population BC but their order is different. Using the function <- compareorder and <- switch.order
I managed, maintaining the similar values of the above-mentioned parameters, unified order of these identical markers on individual groups. I would like to kindly ask you and get to know your opinion: is it acceptable to use these functions until you get the expected result (the same order of markers in some groups), keeping to the right parameters of course (!).
Thank you for your help,
Anna

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] switch.order abuse?
parts:
That sounds acceptable. If you're focusing on finding the order that minimizes the number of observed crossovers, I would try combining the crossover counts between the two crosses. The log likelihoods could also be combined.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] switch.order abuse?
parts:
If you ensure that the two crosses have the same markers in the same order, you could use ripple() on a given chromosome with each cross, and then sum either the LOD scores of the crossover counts.

rip1 <- ripple(cross1, method="countxo", chr=3, window=7)
rip2 <- ripple(cross2, method="countxo", chr=3, window=7)
rip <- rip1
rip[,"obligXO"] <- rip1[,"obligXO"] + rip2[,"obligXO"]
summary(rip)

or for the likelihood method:

rip1 <- ripple(cross1, method="likelihood", chr=3, window=4)
rip2 <- ripple(cross2, method="likelihood", chr=3, window=4)
rip <- rip1
rip[,"LOD"] <- rip1[,"LOD"] + rip2[,"LOD"]
summary(rip)

Alternatively, if you're willing to assume that the recombination rates are the same in the two crosses, you could combine your two 4-way cross objects into one and build the map using the two crosses combined.

karl

The first question concerns the parameters that we take into account when we create linkage groups. Do I do well by choosing a different option (p.ex. - having "shorter" chromosome length) than proposed firstly (“Initial”) by R/qtl? (see the example below in the table)
